subject: chemistry
question_text: Write the IUPAC name and symbol of the element with atomic number 120.

verification.note: PREDICTED, not asked. page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Classification of Elements – Periodic Properties · 2 marks

steps.label: The naming rule
lines: IUPAC rule for elements above Z = 100:
write each digit of the atomic number as a
numerical root and add the ending -ium.
The symbol is the first letter of each root.
steps.why: The name is built digit by digit, so the roots table is the whole method — with it, any atomic number can be named without memorising individual elements.
common_mistakes: Naming the whole number instead of its digits. Each digit gets its own root.
Forgetting the ending -ium after the roots.
steps.memory_tip: Read the atomic number one digit at a time, replace each digit with its root, close with -ium.
steps.margin_note: The roots for 0, 1 and 2 (nil, un, bi) cover most asked cases.

steps.label: The name and symbol

lines.text: Z = 120: un + bi + nil + ium = Unbinilium, symbol Ubn

lines: 1 → un, 2 → bi, 0 → nil, and the ending
The symbol Ubn takes the first letter of each
steps.why: Showing the digit-by-digit build (1, 2, 0 → un, bi, nil) proves the name was derived from the rule and not guessed.
common_mistakes: Writing the symbol with three capital letters. Only the first letter is capital: Ubn.
Dropping the zero. The 0 of 120 contributes the root nil.
steps.memory_tip: 120 spells itself: un-bi-nil plus -ium, and its symbol is the three first letters Ubn.
steps.margin_note: Show the three digits and their roots; the boxed line is then self-checking.

insider_note: The rule is a whole mark, so write the roots out even though the question asks only for a name and a symbol. Showing 1, 2 and 0 becoming un, bi and nil also makes the answer self-checking.
